title: Document desktop controls, control profiles and desk presets
body:
Refs #63.

The accepted 8BitDo desktop-control direction was spread across backlog issues. Add `docs/desktop-controls.md` and README, architecture and roadmap links that record the defaults, qualification questions, command ownership and delivery sequence.

Big A requests Wispr hold-to-dictate without adding send; the first mouse mapping stays scoped to Codex. Work/Free/Quiet desk presets follow Codex-first acceptance and the general-control definition, preserving native device modes and manual ownership. All #63–#71 tickets are linked. Hardware identity, installed app behavior, transport and visible-device acceptance remain distinct.

PC-lighting PR #59 is merged and its separate scope is preserved. Guide inputs and generated HTML now link the document and reflect current backlog data. That refresh discovered #137–#139; their existing scopes have primary coverage and roadmap nodes, with no implementation changes. Existing architecture viewers and source pins are unchanged. Guide #35 will receive the merged document link during completion, preserving #31/#40 ownership and dependencies.

No product behavior or wire-contract delta is introduced, so no new OpenSpec capability is needed. There is no product UI change; the work guide uses the existing SDLC approval exemption. Publication of the public guide is separate.

Validation at `0d558384294d37bb3b9bc8e74137fae3d95a1d69`, from the isolated worktree with Node 24.21.0:

- `npm ci`, `npm run check:workflow`, `npm run test:workflow` passed. Inventory: 10 current specs, 9 archived changes, 15 workflow tests. Current specs are agent-lifecycle-contract, agent-provider-emitters, agent-state-core, controller-contracts, shared-mcp-gateway, shared-monitor-installation, shared-monitor-performance-baseline, standalone-hub-host, standalone-hub-mcp and unified-dashboard.
- All 42 relative Markdown links and anchors across the four documentation files passed; issue/native-dependency and official-reference reads were refreshed.
- `python3 docs/work-guide/work/build_guide.py`, `python3 docs/work-guide/work/test_maintenance.py` and `node docs/work-guide/work/check_guide.cjs` passed. Five maintenance tests, six widths, print expansion/restoration, 96 primary open issues, 12 guides and nine unchanged viewers. Rebuild after commit produced no generated-output drift.
- `git diff --check` passed. Guide SHA-256: `cb3fd4ca3e8ada5335c279459037421ea562b84dae6146c5cfbba7a03475eff6`.

Acceptance mapping: AC1 accepted decisions and dated official sources; AC2 full ticket/dependency map and independent shortcut path; AC3 native-mode/manual-owner boundaries; AC4 evidence table; AC5 fresh-main reconciliation preserving PR #59; AC6 local checks, independent reviews, all six applicable hosted jobs and guarded squash/main verification. Reviews and hosted checks remain pending.

Risk is limited to documentation accuracy and guide freshness. Revert through a normal reviewed PR if needed. Source completion needs merged-main CI, issue closure/readback and a linked guide follow-up for newly confirmed history/status. The public landing page still serves the separately published older edition, hash `4d8f172a5025252c7b06551dfa862d1abe697fc532a54f75151d231217ed799e`.

Delivery strategy: coordinator-authored documentation, then separate read-only Standards and Specification reviewers requested at `gpt-5.6-terra` / `high`. No implementation workers or advisor consultations. Runtime model identity and usage remain unknown unless exposed by the host.

title: Verify bounded standalone cross-device compatibility
body:
Refs #9.

The reduced personal-project scope needs one compatibility check across the standalone Hub, actual dashboard, Pixoo and Nanoleaf. This adds a bounded synthetic runner using pinned owning source, disposable Linux state and fake physical boundaries. Twelve scenarios cover everyday Codex states, two same-project sessions, one Claude smoke, label/monitor acknowledgment, frontend Nanoleaf settings, MCP Pixoo mode, duplicate/late events, a disconnected consumer and restart without obsolete replay.

The existing product and UI code are unchanged. The runner checks native queued/applied receipts, current consumer connections, matching freshness and preserved effect epochs. Failed development attempts are recorded in `docs/cross-device-compatibility.md`; the report refuses overwrites and retains preflight failures. The runner rebuilds both TypeScript sources before importing output and forcibly reaps owned process groups when graceful shutdown fails. Both negative checks run in the required Hub CI suite. It reuses existing detailed contract, MCP and migration tests.

Local validation: Node 24.21.0/Python 3.14.4; 12 source scenarios with cleanup; build/type; 69 Hub tests; 5 dashboard tests and browser/matrix checks; TypeScript/Python controller/lifecycle/state suites; MCP/protocol; packaged Hub; 15 workflow tests; OpenSpec strict validation; guide generation, 5 maintenance tests and browser/print checks. Ten existing specification capabilities remain unchanged; this verification-only change explicitly uses `skip_specs: true`.

Guide inputs and HTML reflect #9's reduced scope and in-progress state. HTML SHA-256: `16b813fe25e7c75307f7faf23cf8056219a2718e45eee7ed63169b0351e705af`. Diagram ownership/flows are unchanged. Public publication is outside scope.

Draft while #30's report in PR #135 awaits delivery. The performance report used its own recorded runtime/pins; it is not relabeled as a timing measurement of #9's settings-capable Nanoleaf revision. Three independent Standards/Specification review rounds resolved all code findings through two correction batches. Final acceptance review after incorporating #30, OpenSpec archive, guarded merge remain pending. All six hosted jobs passed at `48b41a80ebc3fd03ff11206f8bfe10a03a939f00`. No installation, actual agent client, live migration or physical operation occurred.

title: Qualify everyday standalone monitoring with real consumers
body:
Refs #30.

This adds one confined Linux/WSL qualification command for the revised personal-project scope. It uses the delivered hook and Hub, pinned real Pixoo/Nanoleaf consumers, the actual dashboard and fake Pixoo display transport. It covers one/ten-task monitoring, a short 50-task burst, concurrent integration control, consumer/host outages, restart, retained state and exclusive ownership.

The final retained run at `d9f5e7e1129f048f8caee046f8f6644e043ec6e2` passes unchanged predeclared targets: 400 warm events, hook p95 58/78 ms, each consumer receipt p95 below one second, 151 MiB peak Hub RSS and all 487 hooks below 3,000 ms. Preparation and measurement both run in supervised private namespaces with verified cleanup. Dashboard evidence records an observed disconnection, a second feed and post-outage revision 473 in 798 ms. Eight development and four full attempts remain retained, including failures and superseded acceptance evidence. See `docs/performance/standalone-2026-09-22/README.md`, `report.json` and `attempts.json`.

Q1 review found two blockers: preparation outside confinement and an unproven dashboard reconnect. Both are corrected with negative preparation/cache tests and positive reconnect observations. CI then caught npm living outside /usr on hosted runners; the launcher now mounts the selected npm distribution explicitly. Concurrent H137/H138/H139 also required guide coverage/timeline reconciliation. No source target, historical receipt or CI gate was weakened.

Local canonical build/type/contract/lifecycle/state/MCP/Hub/setup/dashboard/workflow checks passed, plus nine Python and four Node qualification tests, 37 pinned Pixoo regressions and 39 Nanoleaf shared-input regressions. Eleven OpenSpec capabilities validate; the new three-requirement/six-scenario change is synchronized and archived. The refreshed guide covers qualification, sequencing and concurrent monitoring issues; generation, five maintenance tests, desktop/mobile/browser/print and output-drift checks passed before this final receipt refresh. Final guide hash/check receipt and fixed-head review results are recorded in the delivery comment.

Renewed independent Standards/Specification review and all six current-head CI jobs are required before guarded squash merge. Merged-main checks precede issue closure. No application UI changes; guide edits use the SDLC exemption. This is source/fake-transport evidence, not installation, client, physical or embedded-host acceptance. Public guide publication remains outside scope and still records source `260707019b7ff83d57e31d91ae1e1582c3734589`.
